answer:
Data is from Trustpilot today (Nov 9, 2026). For each provider I read its roughly 30–55 most recent 1-star reviews (the first 3 pages), not all of them. The complaint categories come from reading plus a rough keyword count, so treat the proportions as approximate.

- NordVPN: 4.2, 51,602 reviews (12% are 1-star). Most common complaint: unexpected auto-renewal or extra charges and refused refunds. Next is not connecting or being blocked.
- ExpressVPN: 4.4, 29,693 reviews (7%). Most common: billing, meaning double charges, charges after cancelling, and refunds denied. Poor support (AI chat, no phone) comes close behind.
- Surfshark: 4.3, 31,815 reviews (9%). Most common: auto-renewal at a much higher price and refused refunds. Sites blocking the VPN and slow speeds are secondary.
- Proton VPN: 2.1, 1,037 reviews (59% are 1-star). Most common: billing and refund disputes, including promo subscriptions turned into credits. Next are slow or failing connections and poor support, which is mostly AI bots.
- CyberGhost: 4.0, 24,173 reviews (7%). Most common: auto-renewal and billing after cancelling. Unreliable connections and bad Linux or streaming support come next.
- Private Internet Access: 4.2, 11,033 reviews (10%). Most common: billing, including renewal without notice, a checkout price above the quoted one, and cashback not honoured. Dropped connections and bad support follow.
- IPVanish: 3.9, 10,307 reviews (6%). Most common: renewal and billing, by a wide margin. This covers auto-renew that can't be turned off, price hikes with no notice, and refund runarounds.
- Mullvad: 3.2, 192 reviews (21%). It has the smallest sample and the most mixed complaints. The leading one is failed or unrecorded payments with no refund and slow, unhelpful support. Others are blocked connections, kill-switch problems and the removal of port forwarding.

The common thread is billing: 1-star reviews for almost every provider are mostly about auto-renewal and refunds, not the VPN itself. Proton VPN is the clear outlier on rating.

Fewest serious complaints: ExpressVPN. It has the highest TrustScore (4.4), the second-lowest 1-star share (7%, against IPVanish's 6%) and a large review base. Its 1-star reviews are mostly billing and support gripes. A few allege serious issues like unauthorized charges and a data-compromise claim, but these are individual accusations I haven't verified. IPVanish and CyberGhost are close behind on 1-star share, but their scores are lower (3.9 and 4.0). Mullvad's 21% is based on only 192 reviews, so it is a weaker signal.

steps.text:
Data is from Trustpilot today (Nov 9, 2026). For each provider I read its roughly 30–55 most recent 1-star reviews (the first 3 pages), not all of them. The complaint categories come from reading plus a rough keyword count, so treat the proportions as approximate.

- NordVPN: 4.2, 51,602 reviews (12% are 1-star). Most common complaint: unexpected auto-renewal or extra charges and refused refunds. Next is not connecting or being blocked.
- ExpressVPN: 4.4, 29,693 reviews (7%). Most common: billing, meaning double charges, charges after cancelling, and refunds denied. Poor support (AI chat, no phone) comes close behind.
- Surfshark: 4.3, 31,815 reviews (9%). Most common: auto-renewal at a much higher price and refused refunds. Sites blocking the VPN and slow speeds are secondary.
- Proton VPN: 2.1, 1,037 reviews (59% are 1-star). Most common: billing and refund disputes, including promo subscriptions turned into credits. Next are slow or failing connections and poor support, which is mostly AI bots.
- CyberGhost: 4.0, 24,173 reviews (7%). Most common: auto-renewal and billing after cancelling. Unreliable connections and bad Linux or streaming support come next.
- Private Internet Access: 4.2, 11,033 reviews (10%). Most common: billing, including renewal without notice, a checkout price above the quoted one, and cashback not honoured. Dropped connections and bad support follow.
- IPVanish: 3.9, 10,307 reviews (6%). Most common: renewal and billing, by a wide margin. This covers auto-renew that can't be turned off, price hikes with no notice, and refund runarounds.
- Mullvad: 3.2, 192 reviews (21%). It has the smallest sample and the most mixed complaints. The leading one is failed or unrecorded payments with no refund and slow, unhelpful support. Others are blocked connections, kill-switch problems and the removal of port forwarding.

The common thread is billing: 1-star reviews for almost every provider are mostly about auto-renewal and refunds, not the VPN itself. Proton VPN is the clear outlier on rating.

Fewest serious complaints: ExpressVPN. It has the highest TrustScore (4.4), the second-lowest 1-star share (7%, against IPVanish's 6%) and a large review base. Its 1-star reviews are mostly billing and support gripes. A few allege serious issues like unauthorized charges and a data-compromise claim, but these are individual accusations I haven't verified. IPVanish and CyberGhost are close behind on 1-star share, but their scores are lower (3.9 and 4.0). Mullvad's 21% is based on only 192 reviews, so it is a weaker signal.
